title: Why you need a good night's sleep
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.term: catching forty winks / getting some shut-eye / dozing / taking a nap

keywords.def: wait until you’ve had time to think carefully before making a decision
an absence or too little of something important eg. food, sleep
changes in the human body in response to a life-threatening situation which make us either stay and fight the threat, or run away from it
cause other results or events, but not directly

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，这里是BBC学英语的《6 Minute English》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Georgie, and we're ready to start, Phil… Phil?!
sentences.zh: 我是Georgie，我们准备开始了，Phil……Phil？！

sentences.en: Oh, sorry, Georgie, I was er, just, catching forty winks … you know, getting some shut-eye, dozing, taking a nap...
sentences.zh: 哦，抱歉，Georgie，我刚刚在……眯一会儿呢……你知道的，闭眼休息一下，打个盹，小睡一下……

sentences.en: I was sleeping! Sleeping at work! Phil, how could you?
sentences.zh: 我在睡觉！在工作时间睡觉！Phil，你怎么能这样？

sentences.en: I know, I know. Sorry, I… I didn’t sleep well last night.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我知道。抱歉，我……我昨晚没睡好。

sentences.en: I'll forgive you this time, but make sure you go to bed early tonight because getting a good night's sleep is incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 这次我原谅你，但今晚一定要早点睡，因为睡个好觉极其重要。

sentences.en: For example, did you know that people who get enough sleep live about five years longer than people who don't?
sentences.zh: 例如，你知道吗，睡眠充足的人比睡眠不足的人大约多活五年？

sentences.en: Wow, so a good night's sleep can lengthen your life.
sentences.zh: 哇，所以睡个好觉能延长寿命。

sentences.en: In this programme, we'll be finding out more about the benefits of sleep, and, as usual, learning some useful new vocabulary as well.
sentences.zh: 在这期节目中，我们将进一步了解睡眠的好处，并且像往常一样，学习一些实用的新词汇。

sentences.en: But first, now that you've woken up, I have a question for you.
sentences.zh: 但首先，既然你已经醒了，我有一个问题要问你。

sentences.en: Do you know how much of the average person's life is spent asleep?
sentences.zh: 你知道普通人一生中有多少时间是在睡眠中度过的吗？

sentences.en: Is it: a) a half? b) a quarter? or, c) a third?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 一半？ b) 四分之一？还是 c) 三分之一？

sentences.en: Hmm, I think we spend about a third of our lives sleeping.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得我们大约有一三的时间都在睡觉。

sentences.en: OK, well I'll reveal the correct answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我在节目结束时公布正确答案。

sentences.en: The question of why humans sleep is not easy to answer.
sentences.zh: 人类为什么要睡觉这个问题并不容易回答。

sentences.en: In terms of evolution, why would it make sense to go unconscious every night, leaving yourself vulnerable to danger?
sentences.zh: 从进化的角度来看，为什么每天晚上失去意识、让自己陷入危险之中会在情理之中呢？

sentences.en: It can only mean that the benefits gained from sleep are huge.
sentences.zh: 这只能说明睡眠带来的好处是巨大的。

sentences.en: Here, science journalist, Ginny Smith, explains some of these benefits to BBC Radio 4 programme, Inside Science: So we've probably all experienced this, that if you've had a bad night sleep and then you try and do some work you just can't concentrate - your brain isn't in the right state to take in new information.
sentences.zh: 在这里，科学记者Ginny Smith在BBC Radio 4的节目《Inside Science》中解释了其中的一些好处：所以我们可能都经历过这一点，如果你前一天晚上没睡好，然后尝试做一些工作，你就会发现根本无法集中注意力——你的大脑并不处于吸收新信息的最佳状态。

sentences.en: But we also need to sleep after we've learnt new things because that's when our brain consolidates the information - takes it from short-term storage to long-term storage, fits it in with other things we already know, that old adage of if you've got a problem sleep on it, your brain does actually work on things during the night, and you can often wake up and have solved the problem in your sleep.
sentences.zh: 但我们在学到新东西后也需要睡觉，因为那是大脑巩固信息的时候——把信息从短期存储转移到长期存储，把它和我们已经知道的其他事情结合起来，就像那句老话说的，如果你遇到了问题，睡一觉再说，你的大脑实际上确实会在夜间处理事情，你经常一觉醒来就会在睡梦中解决问题。

sentences.en: When we sleep, our brains refresh, leaving us feeling rested in the morning.
sentences.zh: 当我们睡觉时，大脑会恢复活力，让我们在早晨感到精神饱满。

sentences.en: But after a bad night's sleep it's more difficult to concentrate.
sentences.zh: 但在没睡好的第二天，就更难集中注意力了。

sentences.en: We can’t take in, or understand, new information.
sentences.zh: 我们无法吸收或理解新的信息。

sentences.en: We also have the saying, if you've got a problem, sleep on it.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一句俗语，如果你遇到问题，睡一觉再说（sleep on it）。

sentences.en: To sleep on it means to delay making a decision until you've had time to think about it.
sentences.zh: “sleep on it”的意思是推迟做决定，直到你有时间去思考它。

sentences.en: But that also turns out to be true scientifically speaking - during sleep, your brain really can work out problems and find solutions.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，从科学角度来看也是如此——在睡眠期间，你的大脑确实能解决问题并找到答案。

sentences.en: But what about the other side of the story?
sentences.zh: 但故事的另一面呢？

sentences.en: What happens when you get too little sleep, or none at all?
sentences.zh: 当你睡眠过少，甚至完全不睡时会发生什么？

sentences.en: Here's Ginny Smith again, talking to BBC Radio 4 programme, Inside Science: Sleep deprivation is a form of stress, and we know that when you are stressed your sort of fight-or-flight response is activated and that causes all these changes in your body that focus on immediate survival over long-term health.
sentences.zh: 听听Ginny Smith再次做客BBC Radio 4节目《Inside Science》时的讲述：睡眠剥夺是一种压力，我们知道当你处于压力下时，你的某种“战斗或逃避”反应会被激活，这会导致你体内发生所有这些变化，让你把重点放在眼前的生存上，而不是长期的健康。

sentences.en: But if we are chronically stressed - money worries, or a stressful job, or something that's going on forever, or life, or chronic sleep deprivation that's causing that level of stress, then you might constantly have a damped down immune system which can then lead to all these knock-on problems.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们长期处于压力之中——比如金钱焦虑、压力大的工作、某种没完没了的事情、生活，或者导致这种压力水平的长期睡眠剥夺，那么你的免疫系统可能会一直处于低迷状态，进而导致所有这些连锁问题。

sentences.en: Having none or too little of something important is known as deprivation.
sentences.zh: 缺乏或几乎没有某种重要东西的情况被称为剥夺（deprivation）。

sentences.en: Sleep deprivation is stressful for the body – so stressful that it activates a fight-or-flight response, changes in the human body in response to a life-threatening situation which make us either stay and fight the threat or run away from it.
sentences.zh: 睡眠剥夺对身体来说压力极大——压力大到足以激活“战斗或逃避”反应，这是人体对生死关头做出的反应，让我们要么留下来与威胁战斗，要么逃离它。

sentences.en: As well as a fight-or-flight response, the stress of not getting enough sleep over a longer period also creates problems including heart disease and a weakened immune system.
sentences.zh: 除了“战斗或逃避”反应，长期睡眠不足带来的压力还会引发一系列问题，包括心脏病和免疫系统受损。

sentences.en: Lack of sleep has these knock-on effects, it causes other things to happen, but not directly.
sentences.zh: 睡眠不足会有这些连锁反应（knock-on effects），它会引发其他事情，但不是直接导致的。

sentences.en: Now do you see why it's so important to get a good night's sleep, Phil?
sentences.zh: 现在你知道为什么睡个好觉如此重要了吧，Phil？

sentences.en: Plus, it will stop you sleeping at work again!
sentences.zh: 另外，这能阻止你再次在工作时睡觉！

sentences.en: Right, I think it's time to reveal the answer to my question.
sentences.zh: 好了，我想是时候公布我的问题答案了。

sentences.en: Yes, you asked me how much of the average person's life is spent asleep, and I said it was about a third.
sentences.zh: 是的，你问我普通人一生中有多少时间在睡眠中度过，我说大约是三分之一。

sentences.en: Which was… the correct answer! Assuming you sleep eight hours a day, the average person will sleep for 229,961 hours in their lifetime or around one third of their life.
sentences.zh: 也就是……正确答案！假设你一天睡八个小时，普通人一生中将有229,961小时在睡觉，或者说占了一生的大约三分之一。

sentences.en: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned starting with the phrases catch forty winks, get some shut-eye, doze and take a nap, all of which mean to sleep.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们回顾一下学到的词汇，首先是 catch forty winks、get some shut-eye、doze 和 take a nap，这些短语的意思都是睡觉。

sentences.en: When someone takes in information, they understand it.
sentences.zh: 当某人 take in 信息时，他们理解了这些信息。

sentences.en: If you have a problem and you sleep on it, you delay making a decision until you’ve had time to think about it.
sentences.zh: 如果你遇到了问题并且 sleep on it，你就会推迟做决定，直到你有时间去思考它。

sentences.en: Deprivation is an absence or too little of something important such as food or sleep.
sentences.zh: Deprivation 是指缺少或几乎没有食物或睡眠等重要东西。

sentences.en: The fight-or-flight response describes changes in the human body in response to a dangerous situation which make us either stay and fight the threat or run away from it.
sentences.zh: “战斗或逃避”反应描述了人体对危险情况做出的反应，使我们能够留下来与威胁战斗或逃跑。

sentences.en: And finally, if something has a knock-on effect,itcauses other results indirectly.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果某事有 knock-on effect（连锁反应），它会间接引发其他结果。

sentences.en: Once again our six minutes are up, but remember to join us again next time for more trending topics and useful vocabulary, here at 6 Minute English.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟节目又要结束了，但请记住下次继续收看我们带来的更多热门话题和实用词汇，就在《6 Minute English》。

sentences.en: Goodbye for now! Bye!
sentences.zh: 今天就到这里，再见！再见！
